system_overview: This specification models a simple key-value store with snapshot isolation semantics, written in PlusCal (an algorithmic language that compiles to TLA+). Transactions operate on local snapshots of the store and use a write-conflict detection mechanism to ensure snapshot isolation. The specification instantiates a client-centric isolation framework to formally verify that the system satisfies snapshot isolation but not full serializability (it can exhibit write-skew anomalies).
actors_and_components: The system consists of a shared key-value store, a set of concurrent transaction processes (each identified by a unique transaction ID), and tracking state for conflict detection. Each transaction process independently takes a snapshot, performs reads and writes on its local copy, and attempts to commit. The specification also integrates a client-centric isolation checking module to verify isolation guarantees.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the shared data store mapping keys to values, (2) the set of currently open (active) transactions, (3) a per-transaction record of keys whose writes were missed (occurred after the transaction took its snapshot), (4) each transaction's local snapshot of the store, (5) each transaction's selected read key set, (6) each transaction's selected write key set, (7) each transaction's log of read and write operations (used for isolation verification), and (8) each transaction's current program phase.
initial_state: The store maps all keys to a designated no-value sentinel. No transactions are open. All missed-write sets are empty. All local snapshots map all keys to the no-value sentinel. Read and write key sets are empty. Operation logs are empty. All transaction processes start at their initial phase.
actions: Each transaction process goes through four sequential phases: (1) Start: the transaction registers itself as active, takes a snapshot of the current store, and non-deterministically selects a non-empty set of keys to read and a non-empty set of keys to write. (2) Read: the transaction reads the values of its selected keys from its local snapshot and logs these as read operations. (3) Update: the transaction writes its own transaction ID as the value for each key in its write set within its local snapshot. (4) Commit: the transaction checks whether any of its write keys overlap with keys written by other transactions since the snapshot was taken (the missed set). If there is no conflict, the transaction commits by removing itself from the active set, updating the missed-write tracking for all remaining active transactions, merging its written keys into the shared store, and logging write operations. If there is a conflict, the transaction aborts without modifying the store. After all transactions complete, the system stutters.
safety_properties: Snapshot isolation: the set of committed transactions must satisfy the snapshot isolation commit test, meaning each transaction can be explained as reading from some consistent state where no conflicting concurrent writes occurred. Type correctness: the store maps keys to valid values (transaction IDs or the no-value sentinel), the active transaction set is a subset of all transaction IDs, and the missed-write tracking maps each transaction to a subset of keys.
liveness_properties: Termination: all transaction processes eventually complete (reach their done state). This is guaranteed by weak fairness on each transaction process.
model_bounds: The key set, transaction ID set, and no-value sentinel are declared as constants. For model checking, typical configurations use two keys and three transaction IDs.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for each transaction process. The specification writes the transaction's own ID as the value for all write operations, simplifying the model while still capturing conflict behavior. The specification notes that serializability is NOT satisfied due to write-skew anomalies, which can be demonstrated by enabling the serializability invariant. The specification suggests as an exercise to add more yield points (smaller atomic actions) to explore what breaks when the commit action is split further.
